questions.subject: science
questions.question: What type of chemical reaction is the reaction between sodium chloride and silver nitrate?
questions.explanation: NaCl and AgNO3 exchange ions. So two new compounds are formed.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What type of reaction is 4Na + O2 -> 2Na2O?
questions.explanation: Sodium and oxygen combine to form one product. So it is a combination reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which substance is X in the reaction HCl + X -> NaCl + H2O?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide. The products are sodium chloride and water.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What type of reaction is the heating of CaCO3?
questions.explanation: Calcium carbonate breaks into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide on heating. So it is a decomposition reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a chemical reaction?
options: Only a change in shape without new substance
A chemical change process involving loss, gain or sharing of electrons to form products
questions.explanation: Chemical reaction forms new substances. It happens due to change in atoms or electrons.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a chemical equation?
options: Representation of reactants and products by words, symbols or formulae
questions.explanation: Chemical equations show reactants and products. They use words, symbols or formulae.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In a chemical equation, what are reactants?
options: Substances formed only at the end
Substances that take part at the beginning of a reaction
questions.explanation: Reactants are substances present at the start. Products are substances formed after reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In a chemical equation, what are products?
questions.explanation: Products are formed after a chemical reaction. Reactants are the starting substances.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the general form of a combination reaction?
questions.explanation: A combination reaction joins reactants together. It forms one product.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a combination reaction?
options: One reactant breaks into many products
Two or more reactants combine to form only one product
questions.explanation: Combination reaction means two or more reactants form one product. So option A is correct.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is an example of combination reaction from the chapter?
questions.explanation: Magnesium and oxygen combine together. They form magnesium oxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the general form of decomposition reaction?
questions.explanation: Decomposition means breaking one compound. It forms simpler products.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a decomposition reaction?
options: Two elements form one product only
One reactant breaks down into two or more products
Acid and base form salt and water only
questions.explanation: Decomposition reaction breaks one reactant. It forms two or more simpler products.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which equation is a decomposition reaction?
questions.explanation: Potassium chlorate breaks into potassium chloride and oxygen. This happens on heating.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a displacement reaction?
options: A reaction in which an atom or radical of one reactant is displaced by another
A reaction in which no atom changes place
questions.explanation: Displacement reaction means one atom or radical is replaced. Another atom or radical takes its place.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many types of displacement reaction are mentioned?
questions.explanation: Displacement reactions are of two types. They are single displacement and double displacement.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens in a single displacement reaction?
options: One element or radical displaces another from a compound
One compound only breaks by heat
questions.explanation: Single displacement replaces one atom or radical. Double displacement exchanges atoms or radicals.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is a single displacement reaction?
questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than hydrogen. So zinc displaces hydrogen from hydrochloric acid.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens in a double displacement reaction?
options: Two new compounds form by mutual exchange of atoms or radicals
A metal burns in oxygen only
questions.explanation: Double displacement means mutual exchange of ions or radicals. Two compounds exchange their parts.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the general form of double displacement reaction?
questions.explanation: In double displacement, two compounds exchange parts. So two new compounds are formed.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which equation is a double displacement reaction?
questions.explanation: BaCl2 and Na2SO4 exchange radicals. So it is a double displacement reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is an acid-base reaction?
options: One reactant breaks into gases only
Acid and base react to form salt and water
questions.explanation: An acid-base reaction forms salt and water. It is also called neutralization.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is an acid-base reaction called neutralization?
options: Acid and base lose their properties and form neutral compounds
questions.explanation: Acid and base neutralize each other. The products are salt and water.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are the products of HCl and NaOH reaction?
questions.explanation: HCl reacts with NaOH to form NaCl and water. So the products are sodium chloride and water.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the rate of chemical reaction?
options: Change of reactants to products per unit time
questions.explanation: Reaction rate means change in reactants or products per unit time. It tells how fast a reaction occurs.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: At the initial stage of a reaction, what is the concentration of products?
questions.explanation: At the beginning, product is not formed yet. So product concentration is zero.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to product concentration as reaction proceeds?
questions.explanation: As reaction goes on, products increase. Reactants decrease because they are used up.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which reaction is fast according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Acid-base reactions are fast. Rusting of iron is a slow reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which process is slow according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Rusting of iron takes a long time. So it is a slow reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a catalyst?
options: A product formed in every reaction
A substance that increases or decreases reaction rate without permanent chemical change
questions.explanation: A catalyst changes reaction rate. It remains chemically unchanged after the reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a positive catalyst?
options: A catalyst that decreases reaction rate
A catalyst that increases reaction rate
questions.explanation: A positive catalyst speeds up a reaction. A negative catalyst slows down a reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is listed as a positive catalyst?
questions.explanation: MnO2 speeds up the reaction. So it is a positive catalyst.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a negative catalyst?
options: A catalyst that always increases rate
A catalyst that decreases reaction rate
questions.explanation: A negative catalyst decreases reaction rate. A positive catalyst increases reaction rate.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which substance is mentioned as a negative catalyst?
questions.explanation: H3PO4 slows down the reaction. So it is a negative catalyst.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does temperature generally affect reaction rate?
options: Rate increases with increase in temperature
questions.explanation: Higher temperature makes particles move faster. So reaction rate increases.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does pressure affect gaseous reactions?
options: Rate increases with increase in gas pressure
questions.explanation: Higher pressure brings gas particles closer. So gaseous reactions become faster.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does surface area affect reaction rate?
options: Greater surface area gives faster reaction
Less surface area always gives faster reaction
questions.explanation: Larger contact surface lets more particles react at once. So reaction rate increases.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which form of vitamin C reacts faster in the surface area activity?
questions.explanation: Powder has larger surface area than a whole capsule. So it reacts faster.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does light affect some chemical reactions?
options: It increases the rate of reactions that need light
It has no role in any reaction
questions.explanation: Some reactions need light. Light can increase their reaction rate.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is hydrogen peroxide not stored in a transparent vessel?
options: Light can increase its decomposition reaction
It needs more oxygen from air
questions.explanation: Light speeds up decomposition of hydrogen peroxide. A transparent vessel lets light enter.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which set contains only factors affecting rate of chemical reaction from the chapter?
options: Catalyst, heat, pressure, surface area, light
Blood group, galaxy, valency, byte, orbit
Only colour, smell, taste and shape
questions.explanation: Catalyst, heat, pressure, surface area and light affect reaction rate. So this set is correct.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In the reaction of copper sulphate with iron nail, what type of reaction occurs?
questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper. So iron displaces copper from copper sulphate.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which balanced reaction represents copper plating on an iron nail?
questions.explanation: Iron reacts with copper sulphate. It forms iron sulphate and copper.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Four students tried reactions: burning Mg, mixing Zn with FeSO4, heating KClO3, and mixing Zn with HCl. Who performed a decomposition reaction?
options: Student D who mixed Zn with HCl
Student B who mixed Zn with FeSO4
questions.explanation: Heating KClO3 breaks it into KCl and O2. So it is a decomposition reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the balanced decomposition of potassium chlorate?
questions.explanation: 2KClO3 -> 2KCl + 3O2 is the balanced equation. Atoms are equal on both sides.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is substance A when magnesium ribbon burns to form white ash?
questions.explanation: Burning magnesium forms white magnesium oxide ash. So substance A is magnesium oxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which balanced reaction shows burning of magnesium?
questions.explanation: Magnesium combines with oxygen. The product is magnesium oxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement best compares combination and decomposition reactions?
options: Both always form salt and water
Combination forms one product; decomposition breaks one reactant into many products
questions.explanation: Combination forms one product. Decomposition breaks one reactant into many products.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement best compares single and double displacement reactions?
options: Both are only caused by light
Both are only breakdown of one compound
Single displacement replaces one atom or radical; double displacement exchanges atoms or radicals between two compounds
questions.explanation: Single displacement replaces one atom or radical. Double displacement exchanges atoms or radicals between two compounds.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does a powdered vitamin C capsule react faster than a whole capsule?
options: Powder has larger surface area of contact
The whole capsule is a catalyst
questions.explanation: Powder has larger surface area. So it reacts faster than a whole capsule.
